note: Questions from the CBSE Class XII Chemistry board exam 2023, Q.P. code 56/1/1, published by CBSE at cbse.gov.in. In the 2023 format the case-based questions were Q31-Q32 and the long answers Q33-Q35; they are tagged here to fit the current layout. Solutions are written for this portal and are not CBSE's official marking scheme.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The colligative property used for the determination of molar mass of polymers and proteins is :
questions.solution: Osmotic pressure is large enough to measure even for very dilute solutions, and is measured at room temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Low concentration of oxygen in the blood and tissues of people living at high altitude is due to :
options: both low temperature and high atmospheric pressure
questions.solution: By Henry's law, the lower partial pressure of oxygen at high altitude reduces its solubility in blood.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The correct cell to represent the reaction Zn + 2Ag⁺ → Zn²⁺ + 2Ag is :
questions.solution: The anode (oxidation, Zn) is written on the left.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: ΔG and E°cell for a spontaneous reaction will be :
questions.solution: ΔG = −nFE: a spontaneous cell has E > 0 and ΔG < 0.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following is affected by a catalyst?
questions.solution: A catalyst provides a path with lower activation energy; it does not change ΔH, ΔG or ΔS.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The order of the reaction H₂(g) + Cl₂(g) —hν→ 2HCl(g) is :
questions.solution: This photochemical reaction is zero order.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The most common and stable oxidation state of a lanthanoid is :
questions.solution: Lanthanoids mainly show +3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The compounds [Co(SO₄)(NH₃)₅]Br and [Co(Br)(NH₃)₅]SO₄ represent :
questions.solution: They exchange the ion inside and outside the coordination sphere, giving different ions in solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The synthesis of alkyl fluoride is best obtained from :
questions.solution: Swartz reaction: heating an alkyl chloride or bromide with a metallic fluoride such as AgF or Hg₂F₂.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: In the reaction R–OH + HCl —ZnCl₂→ RCl + H₂O, what is the correct order of reactivity of alcohols?
questions.solution: The reaction goes through a carbocation, so tertiary alcohols react fastest (the basis of the Lucas test).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: CH₃CONH₂ on reaction with NaOH and Br₂ in alcoholic medium gives :
questions.solution: Hofmann bromamide degradation gives an amine with one carbon fewer: methanamine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following is least basic?
questions.solution: The lone pair on nitrogen in aniline is delocalised into the ring.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The glycosidic linkage involved in linking the glucose units in the amylose part of starch is :
questions.solution: Amylose is a straight chain of α-D-glucose units joined by C1–C4 α-glycosidic links.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: An α-helix is a structural feature of :
questions.solution: The α-helix is a secondary structure of proteins (polypeptides).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The –NH₂ group is o- and p-directing in electrophilic substitution reactions.
Reason (R): Aniline cannot undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Both are true, but the inability to undergo Friedel-Crafts (salt formation with AlCl₃) does not explain o/p direction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A): Acetylation of aniline gives a monosubstituted product.
Reason (R): The activating effect of the –NHCOCH₃ group is more than that of the amino group.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: A is true. R is false: –NHCOCH₃ is less activating than –NH₂, which is why it allows controlled monosubstitution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The molecularity of the reaction H₂ + Br₂ → 2HBr appears to be 2.
Reason (R): Two molecules of the reactants are involved in the given elementary reaction.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: It only appears bimolecular; it is a complex reaction (order 3/2), not an elementary one, so R is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A): Low spin tetrahedral complexes are rarely observed.
Reason (R): Crystal field splitting energy is less than pairing energy for tetrahedral complexes.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Since Δt < P, electrons occupy the higher orbitals rather than pair, giving high-spin complexes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What is Henry's law? Give one application of it.
questions.solution: At constant temperature, the partial pressure of a gas in the vapour phase is proportional to its mole fraction in the solution (p = K_H x); equivalently, its solubility is proportional to its pressure. Applications: soft drinks are bottled under high CO₂ pressure; divers breathe air diluted with helium to avoid the bends.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: On diluting two electrolytes A and B, the Λm of A increases 25 times while that of B increases 1.5 times. Which of the two electrolytes is strong? Justify your answer graphically.
questions.solution: B is strong. For a strong electrolyte Λm rises only slightly on dilution (a nearly straight line with small slope on a Λm vs √c plot); a weak electrolyte's Λm rises sharply at low concentration because its degree of dissociation increases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The electrical resistance of a column of 0.05 mol L⁻¹ NaOH solution of diameter 1 cm and length 50 cm is 5.55 × 10³ ohm. Calculate the conductivity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Complete the following equations : (a) 2MnO₄⁻ + 5NO₂⁻ + 6H⁺ → (b) Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ →
questions.solution: (a) 2MnO₄⁻ + 5NO₂⁻ + 6H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 5NO₃⁻ + 3H₂O. (b) Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Identify A and B in the following reactions : (a) CH₃–CH(OH)–CH₃ —PCl₅→ A —AgCN→ B (b) CH₃CH₂CH₂Cl + KOH (ethanol) → A —HBr→ B
questions.solution: (a) A = 2-chloropropane, CH₃CHClCH₃; B = 2-propyl isocyanide, (CH₃)₂CH–NC (AgCN gives isocyanides). (b) A = propene, CH₃CH=CH₂; B = 2-bromopropane, CH₃CHBrCH₃ (Markovnikov).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Account for the following : (i) Phenol is a stronger acid than an alcohol. (ii) The boiling point of alcohols decreases with increase in branching of the alkyl chain.
questions.solution: (i) The phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance (charge delocalised into the ring); the alkoxide ion is not, and alkyl groups even destabilise it. (ii) Branching makes the molecule more compact, lowering surface area and van der Waals forces.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: (i) Write the mechanism of the reaction CH₃CH₂OH —H⁺, 443 K→ CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O. (ii) Write the equation involved in the Reimer-Tiemann reaction.
questions.solution: (i) Protonation: CH₃CH₂OH + H⁺ → CH₃CH₂OH₂⁺. Loss of water (slow): → CH₃CH₂⁺ + H₂O. Loss of a β-proton: → CH₂=CH₂ + H⁺. (ii) Phenol + CHCl₃ + aq. NaOH (340 K), then H⁺ → salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Explain briefly : (a) Carbylamine reaction (b) Gabriel phthalimide synthesis
questions.solution: (a) Primary amines (aliphatic or aromatic) heated with chloroform and alcoholic KOH give foul-smelling isocyanides: RNH₂ + CHCl₃ + 3KOH → RNC + 3KCl + 3H₂O; used as a test for primary amines. (b) Phthalimide is converted by KOH to potassium phthalimide, which reacts with an alkyl halide to give N-alkylphthalimide; alkaline hydrolysis then gives a pure primary amine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: (a) Write a chemical reaction to show that the open structure of D-glucose contains a straight chain. (b) What type of linkage is responsible for the formation of proteins?
questions.solution: (a) Prolonged heating with HI gives n-hexane, CH₃(CH₂)₄CH₃, showing all six carbons are in a straight chain. (b) The peptide linkage, –CO–NH–.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: (a) Differentiate between an ideal solution and a non-ideal solution. (b) 30 g of urea is dissolved in 846 g of water. Calculate the vapour pressure of water for this solution if the vapour pressure of pure water at 298 K is 23.8 mm Hg.
questions.solution: (a) An ideal solution obeys Raoult's law at all concentrations, with ΔH_mix = 0 and ΔV_mix = 0 (A–B forces equal A–A and B–B). A non-ideal solution deviates from Raoult's law, with ΔH_mix and ΔV_mix not zero. (b) n(urea) = 30/60 = 0.5 mol; n(water) = 846/18 = 47 mol. x(water) = 47/47.5 ≈ 0.989. p = 23.8 × 0.989 ≈ 23.55 mm Hg.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Write the main product formed when : (a) Methyl chloride is treated with NaI/acetone. (b) 2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene is subjected to hydrolysis. (c) n-Butyl chloride is treated with alcoholic KOH.
questions.solution: (a) Methyl iodide, CH₃I (Finkelstein reaction). (b) 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol (picric acid). (c) But-1-ene, CH₃CH₂CH=CH₂.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: How do you convert the following? (Any three) (a) Phenol to picric acid (b) Propanone to 2-methylpropan-2-ol (c) Phenol to anisole (d) Propene to propan-1-ol
questions.solution: (a) Treat with concentrated HNO₃ (often after sulphonation) to give 2,4,6-trinitrophenol. (b) Add CH₃MgBr, then hydrolyse: (CH₃)₂CO → (CH₃)₃C–OH. (c) NaOH to give sodium phenoxide, then CH₃I (Williamson synthesis). (d) Hydroboration-oxidation: B₂H₆, then H₂O₂/OH⁻.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Explain why : (i) The carboxyl group in benzoic acid is meta directing. (ii) Sodium bisulphite is used for the purification of aldehydes and ketones. (iii) Carboxylic acids do not give the characteristic reactions of the carbonyl group.
questions.solution: (i) –COOH is electron-withdrawing and reduces electron density most at the ortho and para positions, so substitution occurs at meta. (ii) Aldehydes and most methyl ketones form crystalline bisulphite addition compounds that can be separated and decomposed back with acid or alkali. (iii) Resonance in –COOH reduces the electrophilic character of the carbonyl carbon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: An organic compound A with molecular formula C₃H₈O, on treatment with Cu at 573 K, gives B. B does not reduce Fehling's solution but gives a yellow precipitate of compound C with I₂/NaOH. Deduce the structures of A, B and C.
questions.solution: B is a methyl ketone formed by dehydrogenation, so A is propan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₃. B = propanone, CH₃COCH₃. C = iodoform, CHI₃ (yellow precipitate).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: (a) What are the hydrolysis products of (i) lactose (ii) maltose? (b) Give the basic structural difference between starch and cellulose.
questions.solution: (a)(i) β-D-galactose and β-D-glucose. (ii) Two molecules of α-D-glucose. (b) Starch is a polymer of α-D-glucose (amylose with C1–C4 α links, amylopectin also with C1–C6 branches); cellulose is a linear polymer of β-D-glucose joined by C1–C4 β-glycosidic links.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
The rate of reaction is concerned with the decrease in concentration of reactants or increase in concentration of products per unit time. It can be expressed as the instantaneous rate at a particular instant or the average rate over a large interval of time. The mathematical representation of the rate of reaction is given by the rate law. The rate constant and order of a reaction can be determined from the rate law or its integrated rate equation.

What is the average rate of reaction?
questions.solution: The change in concentration of a reactant or product divided by the time interval over which it occurs: −Δ[R]/Δt or Δ[P]/Δt.

Write two factors that affect the rate of reaction.
questions.solution: Concentration of reactants, temperature, presence of a catalyst (also surface area, nature of reactants, light).

(1) What happens to the rate of reaction for a zero order reaction? (2) What is the unit of k for a zero order reaction?
questions.solution: (1) The rate stays constant, independent of reactant concentration. (2) mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹.

(1) For a reaction P + 2Q → Products, Rate = k[P]^(1/2)[Q]¹. What is the order of the reaction? (2) Define a pseudo first order reaction with an example.
questions.solution: (1) 1/2 + 1 = 3/2. (2) A reaction that is of higher molecularity but behaves as first order because one reactant is in large excess, e.g. acid hydrolysis of ethyl acetate in excess water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
In coordination compounds, metals show two types of linkages, primary and secondary. Primary valencies are ionisable and are satisfied by negative ions. Secondary valencies are non-ionisable and are satisfied by neutral molecules or negative ions having a lone pair of electrons. Primary valencies are non-directional, while secondary valencies decide the shape of the complexes.

If PtCl₂·2NH₃ does not react with AgNO₃, what will be its formula?
questions.solution: [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂]: both chlorides are in the coordination sphere.

Write the hybridisation and magnetic behaviour of [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻. [Atomic number : Ni = 28]
questions.solution: Ni²⁺ is 3d⁸; strong-field CN⁻ pairs the electrons, giving dsp² hybridisation (square planar) and diamagnetic behaviour.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: (i) State Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions. Write an expression for the limiting molar conductivity of acetic acid according to Kohlrausch's law. (ii) Calculate the maximum work and log K_c for the reaction Ni(s) + 2Ag⁺(aq) ⇌ Ni²⁺(aq) + 2Ag(s) at 298 K. Given : E°(Ni²⁺/Ni) = −0.25 V, E°(Ag⁺/Ag) = +0.80 V, 1 F = 96500 C mol⁻¹.
questions.solution: (i) The limiting molar conductivity of an electrolyte is the sum of the limiting ionic conductivities of its cation and anion. Λ°m(CH₃COOH) = λ°(H⁺) + λ°(CH₃COO⁻) = Λ°m(HCl) + Λ°m(CH₃COONa) − Λ°m(NaCl). (ii) E°cell = 0.80 − (−0.25) = 1.05 V, n = 2. Maximum work = −ΔG° = nFE° = 2 × 96500 × 1.05 = 202650 J ≈ 202.65 kJ. log K_c = nE°/0.0591 = 2 × 1.05/0.0591 ≈ 35.53.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: (i) State Faraday's first law of electrolysis. How much charge, in terms of Faraday, is required for the reduction of 1 mol of Cu²⁺ to Cu? (ii) Calculate the emf of the cell Mg(s) | Mg²⁺ (0.1 M) || Cu²⁺ (0.01 M) | Cu(s) at 298 K. [E°cell = +2.71 V, 1 F = 96500 C mol⁻¹, log 10 = 1]
questions.solution: (i) The mass of substance deposited or liberated at an electrode is directly proportional to the quantity of electricity passed (m = ZIt). Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu needs 2 F. (ii) E = 2.71 − (0.0591/2) log(0.1/0.01) = 2.71 − 0.02955 ≈ 2.68 V.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Assign reasons for each of the following : (i) Manganese exhibits the highest oxidation state of +7 among the 3d series of transition elements. (ii) Transition metals and their compounds are generally good catalysts. (iii) Cr²⁺ is reducing while Mn³⁺, with the same d⁴ configuration, is an oxidising agent. (iv) Zn has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation. (v) Cu⁺ is unstable in aqueous solution.
questions.solution: (i) Mn (3d⁵4s²) can use all seven of its 3d and 4s electrons in bonding. (ii) Variable oxidation states, formation of unstable intermediates and a large surface for adsorption. (iii) Cr²⁺ → Cr³⁺ gives the stable t₂g³ configuration; Mn³⁺ → Mn²⁺ gives the stable half-filled d⁵ configuration. (iv) Zn has a completely filled 3d¹⁰ shell, so no unpaired d electrons are available for metallic bonding. (v) Cu⁺ disproportionates (2Cu⁺ → Cu²⁺ + Cu) because the much larger hydration enthalpy of Cu²⁺ more than offsets its second ionisation enthalpy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: (i) Carry out the following conversions : (1) Ethanal to but-2-en-1-al (2) Propanoic acid to 2-chloropropanoic acid. (ii) An alkene A with molecular formula C₅H₁₀ on ozonolysis gives a mixture of two compounds B and C. Compound B gives a positive Fehling test and also reacts with iodine and NaOH solution. Compound C does not give the Fehling test but forms iodoform. Identify A, B and C.
questions.solution: (i)(1) Aldol condensation with dilute NaOH, then heating: 2CH₃CHO → CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CHO → CH₃CH=CHCHO. (2) Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction: Cl₂ with red phosphorus, then water: CH₃CH₂COOH → CH₃CHClCOOH. (ii) B = ethanal (aldehyde giving iodoform), C = propanone (methyl ketone), so A = 2-methylbut-2-ene, (CH₃)₂C=CHCH₃.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: (i) Distinguish with a suitable chemical test : (1) CH₃COCH₂CH₃ and CH₃CH₂CH₂CHO (2) Ethanal and ethanoic acid. (ii) Write the structure of the oxime of acetone. (iii) Identify A to D: CH₃COOH —PCl₅→ A —H₂/Pd–BaSO₄→ B; B —(i) CH₃MgBr (ii) H₃O⁺→ C; B —LiAlH₄→ D.
questions.solution: (i)(1) Tollens' test: butanal gives a silver mirror; butan-2-one does not (butan-2-one gives the iodoform test). (2) NaHCO₃ test: ethanoic acid gives brisk effervescence of CO₂; ethanal does not (ethanal gives Tollens' test). (ii) (CH₃)₂C=N–OH. (iii) A = CH₃COCl (acetyl chloride); B = CH₃CHO (Rosenmund reduction); C = CH₃CH(OH)CH₃ (propan-2-ol); D = CH₃CH₂OH (ethanol).
